cards.quote: AITUC was a broad-based organisation involving diverse ideologies. The main ideological groups were the communists led by S.A. Dange and M.N. Roy, the moderates led by M. Joshi and V.V. Giri and the nationalist movements which involved people like Lala Lajpat Rai and Jawaharlal Nehru.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: Which union did the Indian National Congress form in May 1947?
cards.back: The Indian National Congress chose to form another union called the Indian National Trade Union Congress (INTUC) in May 1947.
cards.quote: The Indian National Congress chose to form another union called the Indian National Trade Union Congress (INTUC) in May 1947.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: The split in the AITUC in 1947 paved the way for ____ on the line of political parties.
cards.back: The split in the AITUC in 1947 paved the way for further splits on the line of political parties.
cards.quote: The split in the AITUC in 1947 paved the way for further splits on the line of political parties.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: What major workers' strike took place in 1974?
cards.back: In 1974 there was a major railway workers' strike.
cards.quote: In 1974 there was a major railway workers' strike.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: Name what the Dalit movement is a struggle for, in NCERT's words.
cards.back:
recognition as fellow human beings
self-confidence and a space for self-determination
abolishment of stigmatisation, that untouchability implied
cards.quote: This is a struggle for recognition as fellow human beings. It is a struggle for self-confidence and a space for self-determination. It is a struggle for abolishment of stigmatisation, that untouchability implied.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: What has the Dalit struggle against the stigmatisation that untouchability implied been called?
cards.back: It is a struggle for abolishment of stigmatisation, that untouchability implied. It has been called a struggle to be touched.
cards.quote: It is a struggle for abolishment of stigmatisation, that untouchability implied. It has been called a struggle to be touched.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: What does the word Dalit mean?
cards.back: The word Dalit is commonly used in Marathi, Hindi, Gujarati and many other Indian languages, meaning the poor and oppressed persons.
cards.quote: The word Dalit is commonly used in Marathi, Hindi, Gujarati and many other Indian languages, meaning the poor and oppressed persons.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: Who first used the word Dalit in its new context, and when?
cards.back: It was first used in the new context in Marathi by neo-Buddhist activists, the followers of Babasaheb Ambedkar in the early 1970s.
cards.quote: It was first used in the new context in Marathi by neo-Buddhist activists, the followers of Babasaheb Ambedkar in the early 1970s.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: There has not been a ____ Dalit movement in the country now or in the past.
cards.back: There has not been a single, unified Dalit movement in the country now or in the past.
cards.quote: There has not been a single, unified Dalit movement in the country now or in the past.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: Notwithstanding differences in the nature of Dalit movements and the meaning of identity, there has been a common quest for ____, ____ and ____
cards.back: Notwithstanding differences in the nature of Dalit movements and the meaning of identity, there has been a common quest for equality, self-dignity and eradication of untouchability
cards.quote: Notwithstanding differences in the nature of Dalit movements and the meaning of identity, there has been a common quest for equality, self-dignity and eradication of untouchability

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: Name the Dalit movements NCERT cites for the common quest for equality and self-dignity.
cards.back:
Satnami Movement of the Chamars in the Chattisgarh plains in eastern MP
Adi Dharma Movement in Punjab
the Mahar Movement in Maharashtra
the socio-political mobilisation among the Jatavas of Agra
the Anti-Brahman Movement in south India
cards.quote: This can be seen in the Satnami Movement of the Chamars in the Chattisgarh plains in eastern MP, Adi Dharma Movement in Punjab, the Mahar Movement in Maharashtra, the socio-political mobilisation among the Jatavas of Agra and the Anti-Brahman Movement in south India.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: In the contemporary period, the Dalit movement has unquestionably acquired a place in the ____ that cannot be ignored.
cards.back: In the contemporary period, the Dalit movement has unquestionably acquired a place in the public sphere that cannot be ignored.
cards.quote: In the contemporary period, the Dalit movement has unquestionably acquired a place in the public sphere that cannot be ignored.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: Under whose inspiration did the 19th-century anti-caste movement begin (Box 8.7)?
cards.back: the anti-caste movement which began in the 19th century under the inspiration of Jotiba Phule and was carried out in the 1920s by the non-Brahmin movements in Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu and then developed under the leadership of Dr. Ambedkar had characteristics of all types.
cards.quote: the anti-caste movement which began in the 19th century under the inspiration of Jotiba Phule and was carried out in the 1920s by the non-Brahmin movements in Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu and then developed under the leadership of Dr. Ambedkar had characteristics of all types.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: What has the uniting of similarly placed caste groups, under colonial caste-based patronage, been termed?
cards.back: The colonial state often distributed patronage on the basis of caste. It made sense, therefore, for people to stay within their caste for social and political identity in institutional life. It also influenced similarly placed caste groups to unite themselves and to form what has been termed a ‘horizontal stretch’.
cards.quote: The colonial state often distributed patronage on the basis of caste. It made sense, therefore, for people to stay within their caste for social and political identity in institutional life. It also influenced similarly placed caste groups to unite themselves and to form what has been termed a ‘horizontal stretch’.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: Where and since when did the term Backward Classes begin to be used more widely?
cards.back: The term 'Backward Classes' has been in use in different parts of the country since the late 19th Century. It began to be used more widely in Madras presidency since 1872, in the princely state of Mysore since 1918, and in Bombay presidency since 1925.
cards.quote: The term 'Backward Classes' has been in use in different parts of the country since the late 19th Century. It began to be used more widely in Madras presidency since 1872, in the princely state of Mysore since 1918, and in Bombay presidency since 1925.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: The strength of the chain is measured by the ____ link of it and so until every link is fully revitalised, we will not have a healthy body politic.
cards.back: The strength of the chain is measured by the weakest link of it and so until every link is fully revitalised, we will not have a healthy body politic.
cards.quote: The strength of the chain is measured by the weakest link of it and so until every link is fully revitalised, we will not have a healthy body politic.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.note: G.B. Pant said this in his speech on the Advisory Committee (Box 8.8).

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: What reservation did the Government of India introduce in 2019 for economically weaker sections among upper castes?
cards.back: In 2019, the Government of India introduced 10 per cent reservation in education and government jobs for economically weaker sections among upper castes.
cards.quote: In 2019, the Government of India introduced 10 per cent reservation in education and government jobs for economically weaker sections among upper castes.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: Where are many tribal movements largely located, and which tribes are named?
cards.back: Many of the tribal movements have been largely located in the so called 'tribal belt' in middle India, such as the Santhals, Hos, Oraons, Mundas in Chota Nagpur and the Santhal Parganas.
cards.quote: Many of the tribal movements have been largely located in the so called 'tribal belt' in middle India, such as the Santhals, Hos, Oraons, Mundas in Chota Nagpur and the Santhal Parganas.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: From which state and in which year was Jharkhand carved out?
cards.back: Jharkhand is one of the newly formed states of India, carved out of south Bihar in the year 2000.
cards.quote: Jharkhand is one of the newly formed states of India, carved out of south Bihar in the year 2000.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: Who was the charismatic leader of the social movement for Jharkhand?
cards.back: The social movement for Jharkhand had a charismatic leader in Birsa Munda, an adivasi who led a major uprising against the British.
cards.quote: The social movement for Jharkhand had a charismatic leader in Birsa Munda, an adivasi who led a major uprising against the British.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: Who were responsible for spreading literacy in south Bihar, helping the Jharkhand movement?
cards.back: Christian missionaries working in south Bihar were responsible for spreading literacy in the area.
cards.quote: Christian missionaries working in south Bihar were responsible for spreading literacy in the area.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: What did the writings of literate adivasis on their history, myths and customs help create in Jharkhand?
cards.back: Literate adivasis began to research and write about their history and myths. They documented and disseminated information about tribal customs and cultural practices. This helped create a unified ethnic consciousness and a shared identity as Jharkhandis.
cards.quote: Literate adivasis began to research and write about their history and myths. They documented and disseminated information about tribal customs and cultural practices. This helped create a unified ethnic consciousness and a shared identity as Jharkhandis.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: What emerged among literate adivasis with government jobs and lobbied for a separate state in India and abroad?
cards.back: Literate adivasis were also in a position to get government jobs so that, over time, a middle-class adivasi intellectual leadership emerged that formulated the demand for a separate state and lobbied for it in India and abroad.
cards.quote: Literate adivasis were also in a position to get government jobs so that, over time, a middle-class adivasi intellectual leadership emerged that formulated the demand for a separate state and lobbied for it in India and abroad.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: Who were the 'dikus' in south Bihar?
cards.back: adivasis shared a common hatred of dikus – migrant traders and moneylenders who had settled in the area and grabbed its wealth, impoverishing the original residents.
cards.quote: adivasis shared a common hatred of dikus – migrant traders and moneylenders who had settled in the area and grabbed its wealth, impoverishing the original residents.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: Name the issues against which the leaders of the Jharkhand movement agitated.
cards.back:
acquisition of land for large irrigation projects and firing ranges
survey and settlement operations, which were held up, camps closed down, etc.
collection of loans, rent and cooperative dues, which were resisted
nationalisation of forest produce which they boycotted
cards.quote: The issues against which the leaders of the movement in Jharkand agitated were: acquisition of land for large irrigation projects and firing ranges; survey and settlement operations, which were held up, camps closed down, etc. collection of loans, rent and cooperative dues, which were resisted; nationalisation of forest produce which they boycotted

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: What is the rise of ethnicity in the North East a response to?
cards.back: The rise of ethnicity in the region is thus a response to cope with the new situation which developed as a consequence of the tribe’s contact with a powerful alien system.
cards.quote: The rise of ethnicity in the region is thus a response to cope with the new situation which developed as a consequence of the tribe’s contact with a powerful alien system.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: In North East tribal movements, a tendency towards secessionism has been replaced by a search for what?
cards.back: While the earlier phase showed a tendency towards secessionism, this trend has been replaced by a search for autonomy within the framework of the Indian Constitution
cards.quote: While the earlier phase showed a tendency towards secessionism, this trend has been replaced by a search for autonomy within the framework of the Indian Constitution

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: One of the key issues that bind tribal movements from different parts of the country is the ____.
cards.back: One of the key issues that bind tribal movements from different parts of the country is the alienation of tribals from forest lands.
cards.quote: One of the key issues that bind tribal movements from different parts of the country is the alienation of tribals from forest lands.
blanks: alienation of tribals from forest lands

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: Name the early women's organisations NCERT mentions, with years.
cards.back:
Women's India Association (WIA) (1917)
All India Women's Conference (AIWC) (1926)
National Council for Women in India (NCWI) (1925)
cards.quote: The Women's India Association (WIA) (1917), All India Women's Conference (AIWC) (1926) and National Council for Women in India (NCWI) (1925) are ready names of organisations that we can mention.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: For instance, the AIWC began with the idea that 'women's welfare' and 'politics' were ____.
cards.back: For instance, the AIWC began with the idea that 'women's welfare' and 'politics' were mutually exclusive.
cards.quote: For instance, the AIWC began with the idea that 'women's welfare' and 'politics' were mutually exclusive.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: Which features of a social movement did the early women's activity have, according to NCERT?
cards.back:
organisations
ideology
leadership
a shared understanding
the aim of bringing about changes on a public issue
cards.quote: It did have organisations, ideology, leadership, a shared understanding and the aim of bringing about changes on a public issue.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: Name NCERT's examples of women's participation in agrarian and tribal revolts.
cards.back:
The Tebhaga movement in Bengal
the Telangana arms struggle from the erstwhile Nizam's rule
the Warli tribal's revolt against bondage in Maharashtra
cards.quote: Women participated along with men in struggles and revolts originating in tribal and rural areas in the colonial period. The Tebhaga movement in Bengal, the Telangana arms struggle from the erstwhile Nizam's rule, and the Warli tribal's revolt against bondage in Maharashtra are some examples.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: When was the women's movement renewed in India, and what do some call it?
cards.back: In the mid–1970s, there was a renewal of the women's movement in India. Some call it the second phase of the Indian women's movement.
cards.quote: In the mid–1970s, there was a renewal of the women's movement in India. Some call it the second phase of the Indian women's movement.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: Which new issue does NCERT name in the second phase of the women's movement?
cards.back: Apart from organisational changes, there were new issues that were focussed upon. For instance, violence against women.
cards.quote: Apart from organisational changes, there were new issues that were focussed upon. For instance, violence against women.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: Issues of land rights, employment have been fought alongside rights against ____ and ____.
cards.back: Issues of land rights, employment have been fought alongside rights against sexual harassment and dowry.
cards.quote: Issues of land rights, employment have been fought alongside rights against sexual harassment and dowry.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: A ____ would allow both men and women to be free.
cards.back: A gender-just society would allow both men and women to be free.
cards.quote: A gender-just society would allow both men and women to be free.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: Name the two factors on which the idea of a gender-just society is based.
cards.back:
educated women with multiple roles
improved sex ratio
cards.quote: The idea of gender-just society is based upon two important factors -- educated women with multiple roles and improved sex ratio.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: Which Government of India programme is an effort towards a gender-just society?
cards.back: The programme of the Government of India, Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao Yojana is an important effort in the actualisation of a gender-just society.
cards.quote: The programme of the Government of India, Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao Yojana is an important effort in the actualisation of a gender-just society.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: What do social movements change, as they arise because groups seek to change their conditions?
cards.back: They arise because individuals and social groups seek to change their conditions. Thereby, they change both themselves and the society.
cards.quote: They arise because individuals and social groups seek to change their conditions. Thereby, they change both themselves and the society.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: You will realise that the Constitution has the capacity to help people because it is based on the basic norms of ____.
cards.back: You will realise that the Constitution has the capacity to help people because it is based on the basic norms of social justice.
cards.quote: You will realise that the Constitution has the capacity to help people because it is based on the basic norms of social justice.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: Who moved the Directive Principle on Village Panchayats as an amendment in the Constituent Assembly?
cards.back: the Directive Principle on Village Panchayats was moved as an amendment in the Constituent Assembly by K. Santhanam. After forty odd years, it became a Constitutional imperative after the 73rd Amendment in 1992.
cards.quote: the Directive Principle on Village Panchayats was moved as an amendment in the Constituent Assembly by K. Santhanam. After forty odd years, it became a Constitutional imperative after the 73rd Amendment in 1992.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.note: K. Santhanam moved it; it became a Constitutional imperative with the 73rd Amendment in 1992.

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: How have social movements aided courts and authorities in relation to rights and principles?
cards.back: Social movements have also aided the courts and authorities to interpret the contents of rights and principles in keeping with the contemporary understanding on social justice.
cards.quote: Social movements have also aided the courts and authorities to interpret the contents of rights and principles in keeping with the contemporary understanding on social justice.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: What is the essence of law, and what is the essence of justice?
cards.back: The essence of law is its force. Law is law because it carries the means to coerce or force obedience. The power of the state is behind it. The essence of justice is fairness.
cards.quote: The essence of law is its force. Law is law because it carries the means to coerce or force obedience. The power of the state is behind it. The essence of justice is fairness.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.note: Law rests on force (the state backs it); justice rests on fairness.

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: The essence of law is its ____.
cards.back: The essence of law is its force.
cards.quote: The essence of law is its force.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: The essence of justice is ____.
cards.back: The essence of justice is fairness.
cards.quote: The essence of justice is fairness.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: What is the Constitution in relation to rules and authorities, and what is the Indian Constitution to India?
cards.back: Constitution is the basis of all rules and authorities. It is the document that constitutes a nation’s tenets. The Indian Constitution is India’s basic norm.
cards.quote: Constitution is the basis of all rules and authorities. It is the document that constitutes a nation’s tenets. The Indian Constitution is India’s basic norm.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: By what procedures and authorities are all other laws made and implemented?
cards.back: All other laws are made as per the procedures prescribed by the Constitution. These laws are made and implemented by the authorities specified by the Constitution.
cards.quote: All other laws are made as per the procedures prescribed by the Constitution. These laws are made and implemented by the authorities specified by the Constitution.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: The Supreme Court is the highest court and the ____ of the Constitution.
cards.back: The Supreme Court is the highest court and the ultimate interpreter of the Constitution.
cards.quote: The Supreme Court is the highest court and the ultimate interpreter of the Constitution.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: A Fundamental Right includes all that is ____ to it.
cards.back: A Fundamental Right includes all that is incidental to it.
cards.quote: A Fundamental Right includes all that is incidental to it.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: What have the terse words of Article 21 (right to life and liberty) been interpreted as including?
cards.back: The terse words of Article 21 recognising the right to life and liberty have been interpreted as including all that goes into a life of quality, including livelihood, health, shelter, education and dignity.
cards.quote: The terse words of Article 21 recognising the right to life and liberty have been interpreted as including all that goes into a life of quality, including livelihood, health, shelter, education and dignity.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.note: Article 21 covers a life of quality: livelihood, health, shelter, education and dignity.

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: In various pronouncements, different attributes of ‘life’ have been expanded and ‘life’ has been explained to mean more than mere ____.
cards.back: In various pronouncements, different attributes of ‘life’ have been expanded and ‘life’ has been explained to mean more than mere animal existence.
cards.quote: In various pronouncements, different attributes of ‘life’ have been expanded and ‘life’ has been explained to mean more than mere animal existence.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: Name four uses of the Supreme Court’s expanded reading of Article 21.
cards.back:
relief to prisoners subjected to torture and deprivation
release and rehabilitation of bonded labourers
against environmentally degrading activities
primary healthcare and primary education
cards.quote: These interpretations have been used to provide relief to prisoners subjected to torture and deprivation, release and rehabilitation of bonded labourers, against environmentally degrading activities, to provide primary healthcare and primary education.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: In 1993 the Supreme Court held that the Right to Information is part of which Fundamental Right?
cards.back: In 1993 the Supreme Court held that Right to Information is a part of and incidental to the Right to Freedom of Speech and Expression under Article 19(1) (a).
cards.quote: In 1993 the Supreme Court held that Right to Information is a part of and incidental to the Right to Freedom of Speech and Expression under Article 19(1) (a).

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.note: RTI is part of the Right to Freedom of Speech and Expression, Article 19(1)(a).

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: Which Directive Principle did the Supreme Court read into the Right to Equality under Article 14?
cards.back: The Supreme Court read the Directive Principle of Equal Pay for Equal Work into the Fundamental Rights to Equality under Article 14 and has provided relief to many plantation and agricultural labourers and to others.
cards.quote: The Supreme Court read the Directive Principle of Equal Pay for Equal Work into the Fundamental Rights to Equality under Article 14 and has provided relief to many plantation and agricultural labourers and to others.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: What does Panchayati Raj mean literally, and what is its idea?
cards.back: Panchayati Raj translates literally to ‘Governance by five individuals’. The idea is to ensure at the village or grass root level a functioning and vibrant democracy.
cards.quote: Panchayati Raj translates literally to ‘Governance by five individuals’. The idea is to ensure at the village or grass root level a functioning and vibrant democracy.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.note: Literally “governance by five individuals”; it aims at grassroot democracy.

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: ____ translates literally to ‘Governance by five individuals’.
cards.back: Panchayati Raj translates literally to ‘Governance by five individuals’.
cards.quote: Panchayati Raj translates literally to ‘Governance by five individuals’.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: On what grounds is democratic participation hindered in a society with sharp inequalities?
cards.back: in a society where there are sharp inequalities, democratic participation is hindered on grounds of gender, caste and class.
cards.quote: in a society where there are sharp inequalities, democratic participation is hindered on grounds of gender, caste and class.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: Whom have caste panchayats usually represented, and what kind of decisions do they take?
cards.back: But they have usually represented dominant groups. Furthermore, they often held conservative views and often have, and continue to take decisions that go against both democratic norms and procedures.
cards.quote: But they have usually represented dominant groups. Furthermore, they often held conservative views and often have, and continue to take decisions that go against both democratic norms and procedures.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: When the constitution was being drafted, ____ did not find a mention in it.
cards.back: When the constitution was being drafted, panchayats did not find a mention in it.
cards.quote: When the constitution was being drafted, panchayats did not find a mention in it.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: What did Dr. Ambedkar argue about local self-government when the Constitution was being drafted?
cards.back: At the same time, drawing on his own rural experience, Dr. Ambedkar argued that local elites and upper castes were so well entrenched in society that local self-government only meant a continuing exploitation of the downtrodden masses of Indian society.
cards.quote: At the same time, drawing on his own rural experience, Dr. Ambedkar argued that local elites and upper castes were so well entrenched in society that local self-government only meant a continuing exploitation of the downtrodden masses of Indian society.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.note: Ambedkar feared local elites and upper castes would use local self-government to keep exploiting the downtrodden.

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: How did Gandhiji envisage each village, and which ideal model did he see for after independence?
cards.back: The concept of local government was dear to Gandhiji too. He envisaged each village as a self-sufficient unit conducting its own affairs and saw gram-swarajya to be an ideal model to be continued after independence.
cards.quote: The concept of local government was dear to Gandhiji too. He envisaged each village as a self-sufficient unit conducting its own affairs and saw gram-swarajya to be an ideal model to be continued after independence.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: Which Constitutional Amendment ushered in grassroot democracy in 1992, and what did it give the PRIs?
cards.back: It was, however, only in 1992 that grassroot democracy or decentralised governance was ushered in by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment. This act provided constitutional status to the Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs).
cards.quote: It was, however, only in 1992 that grassroot democracy or decentralised governance was ushered in by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment. This act provided constitutional status to the Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs).

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: How often must local self-government bodies in rural and municipal areas be elected, and what control do they get?
cards.back: It is compulsory now for local self-government bodies in rural and municipal areas to be elected every five years. More importantly, control of local resources is given to the elected local bodies.
cards.quote: It is compulsory now for local self-government bodies in rural and municipal areas to be elected every five years. More importantly, control of local resources is given to the elected local bodies.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: What is the Gram Sabha in the three-tier Panchayati Raj structure?
cards.back: At the base of the structure stands the unit of democracy or Gram Sabha. This consists of the entire body of citizens in a village or grama. It is this general body that elects the local government and charges it with specific responsibilities.
cards.quote: At the base of the structure stands the unit of democracy or Gram Sabha. This consists of the entire body of citizens in a village or grama. It is this general body that elects the local government and charges it with specific responsibilities.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India
source.section: Box 3.2: The three-tier system of Panchayati Raj

cards.note: The Gram Sabha is the base of the pyramid: all citizens of a village, who elect the local government.

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: What ought Gram Sabhas ideally to provide, and what role should they play?
cards.back: The Gram Sabhas ideally ought to provide an open forum for discussions and village-level development activities and play a crucial role in ensuring inclusion of the weaker sections in the decision-making processes.
cards.quote: The Gram Sabhas ideally ought to provide an open forum for discussions and village-level development activities and play a crucial role in ensuring inclusion of the weaker sections in the decision-making processes.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India
source.section: Box 3.2: The three-tier system of Panchayati Raj

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: The 73rd Amendment provided a three-tier Panchayati Raj for states with what population?
cards.back: The 73rd Amendment provided a three-tier system of Panchayati Raj for all states having a population of over twenty lakhs.
cards.quote: The 73rd Amendment provided a three-tier system of Panchayati Raj for all states having a population of over twenty lakhs.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India
source.section: Box 3.2: The three-tier system of Panchayati Raj

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: Name the four provisions of the 73rd Amendment listed in Box 3.2.
cards.back:
The 73rd Amendment provided a three-tier system of Panchayati Raj for all states having a population of over twenty lakhs.
It became mandatory that election to these bodies be conducted every five years.
It provided reservation of seats for the Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and thirty three percent seats for women.
It constituted District Planning Committee to prepare drafts and develop plans for the district as a whole.
cards.quote: The 73rd Amendment provided a three-tier system of Panchayati Raj for all states having a population of over twenty lakhs. It became mandatory that election to these bodies be conducted every five years. It provided reservation of seats for the Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and thirty three percent seats for women. It constituted District Planning Committee to prepare drafts and develop plans for the district as a whole.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India
source.section: Box 3.2: The three-tier system of Panchayati Raj

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: What reservation of seats did the 73rd Amendment provide for women, besides seats for SCs and STs?
cards.back: It provided reservation of seats for the Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and thirty three percent seats for women.
cards.quote: It provided reservation of seats for the Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and thirty three percent seats for women.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India
source.section: Box 3.2: The three-tier system of Panchayati Raj

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: What did the 73rd Amendment constitute to prepare drafts and develop plans for the district as a whole?
cards.back: It constituted District Planning Committee to prepare drafts and develop plans for the district as a whole.
cards.quote: It constituted District Planning Committee to prepare drafts and develop plans for the district as a whole.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India
source.section: Box 3.2: The three-tier system of Panchayati Raj

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: What reservation for women did the 73rd and 74th amendments ensure in local bodies?
cards.back: The 73rd and 74th amendments to the Constitution ensured the reservation of one third of the total seats for women in all elected offices of local bodies in both the rural and urban areas. Out of this, 17 per cent seats are reserved for women belonging to the scheduled castes and tribes.
cards.quote: The 73rd and 74th amendments to the Constitution ensured the reservation of one third of the total seats for women in all elected offices of local bodies in both the rural and urban areas. Out of this, 17 per cent seats are reserved for women belonging to the scheduled castes and tribes.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: Why is the amendment on women’s reservation in local bodies significant?
cards.back: This amendment is significant as for the first time it brought women into elected bodies which also bestowed on them decision making powers.
cards.quote: This amendment is significant as for the first time it brought women into elected bodies which also bestowed on them decision making powers.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: How many women did the 1993–94 elections bring into the political processes in a single election?
cards.back: The 1993–94 elections, soon after the 73rd amendment brought in 800,000 women into the political processes in a single election.
cards.quote: The 1993–94 elections, soon after the 73rd amendment brought in 800,000 women into the political processes in a single election.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: Name the social welfare responsibilities of the Panchayats.
cards.back:
maintenance of burning and burial grounds
recording statistics of births and deaths
establishment of child welfare and maternity centres
control of cattle pounds
propagation of family planning and promotion of agricultural activities
cards.quote: Social welfare responsibilities of the Panchayats include the maintenance of burning and burial grounds, recording statistics of births and deaths, establishment of child welfare and maternity centres, control of cattle pounds, propagation of family planning and promotion of agricultural activities.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: Name the development activities of the Panchayats.
cards.back:
construction of roads, public buildings, wells, tanks and schools
small cottage industries
minor irrigation works
cards.quote: The development activities include the construction of roads, public buildings, wells, tanks and schools. They also promote small cottage industries and take care of minor irrigation works.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: Name the sources of income of the Panchayats.
cards.back:
tax levied on property, profession, animals, vehicles
cess on land revenue and rentals
grants received through the Zilla Panchayat
cards.quote: The main income of the Panchayats is from tax levied on property, profession, animals, vehicles, cess on land revenue and rentals. The resources are further increased by the grants received through the Zilla Panchayat.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: What is it compulsory for Panchayat offices to put up outside their offices?
cards.back: It is also considered compulsory for Panchayat offices to put up boards outside their offices, listing the break up of funds received, and utilisation of the financial aid received.
cards.quote: It is also considered compulsory for Panchayat offices to put up boards outside their offices, listing the break up of funds received, and utilisation of the financial aid received.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: What authority do Nyaya Panchayats possess, and what can they not do?
cards.back: Nyaya Panchayats have been constituted in some states. They possess the authority to hear some petty, civil and criminal cases. They can impose fines but cannot award a sentence.
cards.quote: Nyaya Panchayats have been constituted in some states. They possess the authority to hear some petty, civil and criminal cases. They can impose fines but cannot award a sentence.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.note: Nyaya Panchayats hear petty civil and criminal cases and can fine, but cannot sentence.

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: In what have Nyaya Panchayats (village courts) been particularly effective?
cards.back: These village courts have often been successful in bringing about an agreement amongst contending parties. They have been particularly effective in punishing men who harass women for dowry and perpetrate violence against them.
cards.quote: These village courts have often been successful in bringing about an agreement amongst contending parties. They have been particularly effective in punishing men who harass women for dowry and perpetrate violence against them.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: What do members of the van-panchayats in Uttarakhand do?
cards.back: Members of the van-panchayats develop nurseries and nurture tree saplings for planting on the hill slopes. Members also police nearby forests to keep an eye on illegal felling of trees.
cards.quote: Members of the van-panchayats develop nurseries and nurture tree saplings for planting on the hill slopes. Members also police nearby forests to keep an eye on illegal felling of trees.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: In the area of Uttarakhand’s van-panchayats, which movement began where women hugged trees to prevent felling?
cards.back: The Chipko movement, where women hugged trees to prevent them from being cut, had its beginnings in this area.
cards.quote: The Chipko movement, where women hugged trees to prevent them from being cut, had its beginnings in this area.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: Which three major ethnic tribal groups of Meghalaya have their own traditional political institutions?
cards.back: All the three major ethnic tribal groups, namely, the Khasis, Jaintias and the Garos have their own traditional political institutions that have existed for hundreds of years.
cards.quote: All the three major ethnic tribal groups, namely, the Khasis, Jaintias and the Garos have their own traditional political institutions that have existed for hundreds of years.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: Why may a large chunk of tribal areas lie outside the provisions of the 73rd Amendment?
cards.back: Though there is a long tradition of grassroot political institutions in Meghalaya, a large chunk of tribal areas lie outside the provisions of the 73rd Amendment. This may be because the concerned policymakers did not wish to interfere with the traditional tribal institutions.
cards.quote: Though there is a long tradition of grassroot political institutions in Meghalaya, a large chunk of tribal areas lie outside the provisions of the 73rd Amendment. This may be because the concerned policymakers did not wish to interfere with the traditional tribal institutions.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: What does sociologist Tiplut Nongbri remark about tribal institutions?
cards.back: However, as sociologist Tiplut Nongbri remarks that tribal institutions in themselves need not necessarily be democratic in its structure and functioning.
cards.quote: However, as sociologist Tiplut Nongbri remarks that tribal institutions in themselves need not necessarily be democratic in its structure and functioning.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: What marks tribal political institutions, and what has social change introduced into them?
cards.back: Tribal political institutions are not only marked by open intolerance to women but the process of social change has also introduced sharp distortions in the system, making it difficult to identify which is traditional and which is not.
cards.quote: Tribal political institutions are not only marked by open intolerance to women but the process of social change has also introduced sharp distortions in the system, making it difficult to identify which is traditional and which is not.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: Democratisation is not easy in a society with a long history of inequality based on which three things?
cards.back: democratisation is not easy in a society that has had a long history of inequality based on caste, community and gender.
cards.quote: It will be clear to you that democratisation is not easy in a society that has had a long history of inequality based on caste, community and gender.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: By whom are Gram Sabha members often controlled, and what is left to the silent majority?
cards.back: The Gram Sabha members are often controlled by a small coterie of rich landlords usually hailing from the upper castes or landed peasantry. They make decisions on development activities, allocate funds, leaving the silent majority as mere onlookers.
cards.quote: The Gram Sabha members are often controlled by a small coterie of rich landlords usually hailing from the upper castes or landed peasantry. They make decisions on development activities, allocate funds, leaving the silent majority as mere onlookers.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: Industrialists, workers and farmers form organisations to be heard: name the NCERT examples.
cards.back:
Industrialists form associations such as Federation of Indian Chambers and Commerce (FICCI) and Association of Chambers of Commerce (ASSOCHAM).
Workers form trade unions such as the Indian Trade Union Congress (INTUC) or the Centre for Indian Trade Unions (CITU).
Farmers form agricultural unions such as Shetkari Sangathan.
cards.quote: Industrialists form associations such as Federation of Indian Chambers and Commerce (FICCI) and Association of Chambers of Commerce (ASSOCHAM). Workers form trade unions such as the Indian Trade Union Congress (INTUC) or the Centre for Indian Trade Unions (CITU). Farmers form agricultural unions such as Shetkari Sangathan.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India
source.section: Political Parties, Pressure and Interest Groups in Democratic Politics

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: Define a political party as an organisation with the aim of achieving governmental power.
cards.back: Political Party is an organisation established with the aim of achieving governmental power and using that power to pursue a specific programme.
cards.quote: Political Party is an organisation established with the aim of achieving governmental power and using that power to pursue a specific programme.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India
source.section: Political Parties, Pressure and Interest Groups in Democratic Politics

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: What may groups do when they feel their interests are not being taken up?
cards.back: When certain groups feel that their interests are not being taken up, they may move to form an alternative party. Or they form pressure groups who lobby with the government.
cards.quote: When certain groups feel that their interests are not being taken up, they may move to form an alternative party. Or they form pressure groups who lobby with the government.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India
source.section: Political Parties, Pressure and Interest Groups in Democratic Politics

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: What are Interest Groups?
cards.back: Interest Groups are organised to pursue specific interests in the political arena, operating primarily by lobbying the members of legislative bodies.
cards.quote: Interest Groups are organised to pursue specific interests in the political arena, operating primarily by lobbying the members of legislative bodies.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India
source.section: Political Parties, Pressure and Interest Groups in Democratic Politics

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: How are political organisations that seek power but are denied standard means best regarded?
cards.back: In some situations, there may be political organisations which seek to achieve power but are denied the opportunity to do so through standard means. These organisations are best regarded as movements until they achieve recognition.
cards.quote: In some situations, there may be political organisations which seek to achieve power but are denied the opportunity to do so through standard means. These organisations are best regarded as movements until they achieve recognition.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India
source.section: Political Parties, Pressure and Interest Groups in Democratic Politics

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: What do some argue the concept of pressure groups underestimates?
cards.back: Some, therefore, argue that the concept of pressure groups underestimate the power that dominant social groups such as class, caste or gender have in society. They feel that it would be more accurate to suggest that dominant class or classes control the state.
cards.quote: Some, therefore, argue that the concept of pressure groups underestimate the power that dominant social groups such as class, caste or gender have in society. They feel that it would be more accurate to suggest that dominant class or classes control the state.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: Max Weber: the place of classes, status groups and parties?
cards.back: Whereas the genuine place of classes is within the economic order, the place of status groups is within the social order…But parties live in a house of power…
cards.quote: Whereas the genuine place of classes is within the economic order, the place of status groups is within the social order…But parties live in a house of power…

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.front: Max Weber: the two kinds of goal a party may have.
cards.back:
‘cause’ (the party may aim at realising a program for ideal or material purposes)
‘personal’ (sinecures, power, and from these, honour for the leader and followers of the party)
cards.quote: Party actions are always directed towards a goal which is striven for in a planned manner. The goal may be a ‘cause’ (the party may aim at realising a program for ideal or material purposes), or the goal may be ‘personal’ (sinecures, power, and from these, honour for the leader and followers of the party).

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.unit: Process of Social Change in India
cards.front: What does colonialism simply mean, at one level?
cards.back: At one level, colonialism simply means the establishment of rule by one country over another.
cards.quote: At one level, colonialism simply means the establishment of rule by one country over another.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.unit: Process of Social Change in India
cards.front: Apart from outright pillage, the pre-capitalist conquerors benefited from their domination by exacting a continuous flow of ____.
cards.back: Apart from outright pillage, the pre-capitalist conquerors benefited from their domination by exacting a continuous flow of tribute.
cards.quote: Apart from outright pillage, the pre-capitalist conquerors benefited from their domination by exacting a continuous flow of tribute.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.note: They did not interfere with the economic base; they took the tribute skimmed off the traditional surplus.

cards.subject: sociology
cards.unit: Process of Social Change in India
cards.front: How did British colonialism interfere in India? NCERT's instances.
cards.back:
For instance it changed the very laws of the land.
It changed not just land ownership laws but decided even what crops ought to be grown and what ought not to be.
It meddled with the manufacturing sector.
It altered the way production and distribution of goods took place.
It entered into the forests.
It cleared trees and started tea plantations.
It brought in Forest Acts that changed the lives of pastoralists.
cards.quote: For instance it changed the very laws of the land. It changed not just land ownership laws but decided even what crops ought to be grown and what ought not to be. It meddled with the manufacturing sector. It altered the way production and distribution of goods took place. It entered into the forests. It cleared trees and started tea plantations. It brought in Forest Acts that changed the lives of pastoralists.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.unit: Process of Social Change in India
cards.front: British colonial rule brought in Forest Acts that changed the lives of which group?
cards.back: It brought in Forest Acts that changed the lives of pastoralists. They were prevented from entering many forests that had earlier provided valuable forage for their cattle.
cards.quote: It brought in Forest Acts that changed the lives of pastoralists. They were prevented from entering many forests that had earlier provided valuable forage for their cattle.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.unit: Process of Social Change in India
cards.front: Colonialism moved people within India: from which present-day region did people go to work in Assam's tea plantations?
cards.back: For instance people from present day Jharkhand moved to Assam to work on the tea plantations.
cards.quote: For instance people from present day Jharkhand moved to Assam to work on the tea plantations.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.unit: Process of Social Change in India
cards.front: Which British Presidency regions did the new middle class of government employees, doctors and lawyers come from?
cards.back: A newly emerging middle class particularly from the British Presidency regions of Bengal and Madras moved as government employees and professionals like doctors and lawyers moved to different parts of the country.
cards.quote: A newly emerging middle class particularly from the British Presidency regions of Bengal and Madras moved as government employees and professionals like doctors and lawyers moved to different parts of the country.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.unit: Process of Social Change in India
cards.front: Box 1.1: where did ships carry people from Indian ports between 1834 and 1920, and for how long?
cards.back: After 1834 till 1920, ships left from the ports of India on regular basis carrying people of various religions, gender, classes and castes destined to work for a minimum of five years on one of the plantations in Mauritius.
cards.quote: After 1834 till 1920, ships left from the ports of India on regular basis carrying people of various religions, gender, classes and castes destined to work for a minimum of five years on one of the plantations in Mauritius.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.unit: Process of Social Change in India
cards.front: Some of these changes were ____ while some took place in an ____ fashion.
cards.back: Some of these changes were deliberate while some took place in an unintended fashion.
cards.quote: Some of these changes were deliberate while some took place in an unintended fashion.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.unit: Process of Social Change in India
cards.front: What is capitalism?
cards.back: Capitalism is an economic system in which the means of production are privately owned and organised to accumulate profits within a market system.
cards.quote: Capitalism is an economic system in which the means of production are privately owned and organised to accumulate profits within a market system.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.unit: Process of Social Change in India
cards.front: What marked capitalism from the very beginning, and what else marked it?
cards.back: What marked capitalism from the very beginning was its dynamism, its potential to grow, expand, innovate, use technology and labour in a way best assured to ensure greatest profit. What marked it too was its global nature.
cards.quote: What marked capitalism from the very beginning was its dynamism, its potential to grow, expand, innovate, use technology and labour in a way best assured to ensure greatest profit. What marked it too was its global nature.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.unit: Process of Social Change in India
cards.front: Capitalism in the west emerged out of which complex process?
cards.back: Capitalism in the west emerged out of a complex process of European exploration of the rest of the world, its plunder of wealth and resources, an unprecedented growth of science and technology, its harnessing to industries and agriculture.
cards.quote: Capitalism in the west emerged out of a complex process of European exploration of the rest of the world, its plunder of wealth and resources, an unprecedented growth of science and technology, its harnessing to industries and agriculture.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.unit: Process of Social Change in India
cards.front: If capitalism became the dominant economic system, ____ became the dominant political form.
cards.back: If capitalism became the dominant economic system, nation states became the dominant political form.
cards.quote: If capitalism became the dominant economic system, nation states became the dominant political form.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.unit: Process of Social Change in India
cards.front: What is a nation state?
cards.back: Nation state pertains to a particular type of state, characteristic of the modern world. A government has sovereign power within a defined territorial area, and the people are citizens of a single nation.
cards.quote: Nation state pertains to a particular type of state, characteristic of the modern world. A government has sovereign power within a defined territorial area, and the people are citizens of a single nation.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.unit: Process of Social Change in India
cards.front: Nation states are closely associated with the rise of ____.
cards.back: Nation states are closely associated with the rise of nationalism.
cards.quote: Nation states are closely associated with the rise of nationalism.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.unit: Process of Social Change in India
cards.front: What does the principle of nationalism assume?
cards.back: The principle of nationalism assumes that any set of people have a right to be free and exercise sovereign power.
cards.quote: The principle of nationalism assumes that any set of people have a right to be free and exercise sovereign power.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.unit: Process of Social Change in India
cards.front: What did Indian nationalist leaders declare about freedom or swaraj?
cards.back: Indian nationalist leaders were quick to grasp this irony. They declared that freedom or swaraj was their birthright and fought for both political and economic freedom.
cards.quote: Indian nationalist leaders were quick to grasp this irony. They declared that freedom or swaraj was their birthright and fought for both political and economic freedom.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India

cards.subject: sociology
cards.unit: Process of Social Change in India
cards.front: What does industrialisation refer to?
cards.back: Industrialisation refers to the emergence of machine production, based on the use of inanimate power resources like steam or electricity.
cards.quote: Industrialisation refers to the emergence of machine production, based on the use of inanimate power resources like steam or electricity.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India
source.section: 1.2 Urbanisation and Industrialisation: The Colonial Experience

cards.subject: sociology
cards.unit: Process of Social Change in India
cards.front: In industrial societies today, where does a large majority of the employed population work?
cards.back: By contrast, a prime feature of industrial societies today is that a large majority of the employed population work in factories, offices or shops rather than agriculture.
cards.quote: By contrast, a prime feature of industrial societies today is that a large majority of the employed population work in factories, offices or shops rather than agriculture.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India
source.section: 1.2 Urbanisation and Industrialisation: The Colonial Experience

cards.subject: sociology
cards.unit: Process of Social Change in India
cards.front: Not surprisingly, therefore, we usually associate urbanisation with industrialisation. They often do occur together but ____.
cards.back: Not surprisingly, therefore, we usually associate urbanisation with industrialisation. They often do occur together but not always so.
cards.quote: Not surprisingly, therefore, we usually associate urbanisation with industrialisation. They often do occur together but not always so.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India
source.section: 1.2 Urbanisation and Industrialisation: The Colonial Experience

cards.subject: sociology
cards.unit: Process of Social Change in India
cards.front: Which society was the first to undergo industrialisation and the earliest to become predominantly urban?
cards.back: For instance in Britain, the first society to undergo industrialisation, was also the earliest to move from being rural to a predominantly urban country.
cards.quote: For instance in Britain, the first society to undergo industrialisation, was also the earliest to move from being rural to a predominantly urban country.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India
source.section: 1.2 Urbanisation and Industrialisation: The Colonial Experience

cards.subject: sociology
cards.unit: Process of Social Change in India
cards.front: In India the impact of the very same British industrialisation led to ____ in some sectors, and decline of old urban centres.
cards.back: In India the impact of the very same British industrialisation led to deindustrialisation in some sectors, and decline of old urban centres.
cards.quote: In India the impact of the very same British industrialisation led to deindustrialisation in some sectors, and decline of old urban centres.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India
source.section: 1.2 Urbanisation and Industrialisation: The Colonial Experience

cards.subject: sociology
cards.unit: Process of Social Change in India
cards.front: Just as manufacturing boomed in Britain, traditional exports of cotton and silk manufactures from India declined in the face of ____.
cards.back: Just as manufacturing boomed in Britain, traditional exports of cotton and silk manufactures from India declined in the face of Manchester competition.
cards.quote: Just as manufacturing boomed in Britain, traditional exports of cotton and silk manufactures from India declined in the face of Manchester competition.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India
source.section: 1.2 Urbanisation and Industrialisation: The Colonial Experience

cards.subject: sociology
cards.unit: Process of Social Change in India
cards.front: Which cities declined and which grew in the colonial period (NCERT's examples)?
cards.back: This period also saw the further decline of cities such as Surat and Masulipatnam while Bombay and Madras grew.
cards.quote: This period also saw the further decline of cities such as Surat and Masulipatnam while Bombay and Madras grew.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India
source.section: 1.2 Urbanisation and Industrialisation: The Colonial Experience

cards.subject: sociology
cards.unit: Process of Social Change in India
cards.front: Which towns lost their courts, artisans and court gentry when the British took over Indian states?
cards.back: When the British took over Indian states, towns like Thanjavur, Dhaka, and Murshidabad lost their courts and, therefore, some of their artisans and court gentry.
cards.quote: When the British took over Indian states, towns like Thanjavur, Dhaka, and Murshidabad lost their courts and, therefore, some of their artisans and court gentry.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India
source.section: 1.2 Urbanisation and Industrialisation: The Colonial Experience

cards.subject: sociology
cards.unit: Process of Social Change in India
cards.front: From the end of the 19th century, with the installation of ____, some towns became much more heavily populated.
cards.back: From the end of the 19th century, with the installation of mechanised factory industries, some towns became much more heavily populated.
cards.quote: From the end of the 19th century, with the installation of mechanised factory industries, some towns became much more heavily populated.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India
source.section: 1.2 Urbanisation and Industrialisation: The Colonial Experience

cards.subject: sociology
cards.unit: Process of Social Change in India
cards.front: Sarkar 1983: village crafts in the interior survived longer; what finally seriously affected them?
cards.back: Village crafts in the interior, and particularly, in regions other than eastern India where British penetration was earliest and deepest, probably survived much longer, coming to be seriously affected only with the spread of railways.
cards.quote: Village crafts in the interior, and particularly, in regions other than eastern India where British penetration was earliest and deepest, probably survived much longer, coming to be seriously affected only with the spread of railways.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India
source.section: 1.2 Urbanisation and Industrialisation: The Colonial Experience

cards.note: Sarkar 1983: village crafts survived longer than urban luxury manufactures.

cards.subject: sociology
cards.unit: Process of Social Change in India
cards.front: Box 1.2 (Census of India Report, 1911): what did cheap European piecegoods and Western-type factories do to village industries?
cards.back: The extensive importation of cheap European piecegoods and utensils, and the establishment in India itself of numerous factories of the Western type, have more or less destroyed many village industries.
cards.quote: The extensive importation of cheap European piecegoods and utensils, and the establishment in India itself of numerous factories of the Western type, have more or less destroyed many village industries.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India
source.section: 1.2 Urbanisation and Industrialisation: The Colonial Experience

cards.note: Box 1.2, Census of India Report, 1911.

cards.subject: sociology
cards.unit: Process of Social Change in India
cards.front: Box 1.3: industrialisation is not just about machine based production but also a story of what?
cards.back: It also shows how industrialisation is not just about new machine based production but also a story of the growth of new social groups in society and new social relationships.
cards.quote: It also shows how industrialisation is not just about new machine based production but also a story of the growth of new social groups in society and new social relationships.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India
source.section: 1.2 Urbanisation and Industrialisation: The Colonial Experience

cards.subject: sociology
cards.unit: Process of Social Change in India
cards.front: Box 1.3 (Mukherjee 1979): what substitutes did the East India Company and British government offer?
cards.back: The substitutes offered by the East India Company and subsequently by the British government were land ownership and facilities for education in English.
cards.quote: The substitutes offered by the East India Company and subsequently by the British government were land ownership and facilities for education in English.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India
source.section: 1.2 Urbanisation and Industrialisation: The Colonial Experience

cards.subject: sociology
cards.unit: Process of Social Change in India
cards.front: Why were coastal cities such as Mumbai, Kolkata and Chennai favoured in the colonial economy?
cards.back: Coastal cities such as Mumbai, Kolkata and Chennai were favoured. From here primary commodities could be easily exported and manufactured goods could be cheaply imported.
cards.quote: Coastal cities such as Mumbai, Kolkata and Chennai were favoured. From here primary commodities could be easily exported and manufactured goods could be cheaply imported.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India
source.section: 1.2 Urbanisation and Industrialisation: The Colonial Experience

cards.subject: sociology
cards.unit: Process of Social Change in India
cards.front: Colonial cities were the prime link between the economic centre or ____ in Britain and ____ or margins in colonised India.
cards.back: Colonial cities were the prime link between the economic centre or core in Britain and periphery or margins in colonised India.
cards.quote: Colonial cities were the prime link between the economic centre or core in Britain and periphery or margins in colonised India.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India
source.section: 1.2 Urbanisation and Industrialisation: The Colonial Experience

cards.subject: sociology
cards.unit: Process of Social Change in India
cards.front: Colonial exports: what was shipped through Bombay, Calcutta and Madras?
cards.back: In British India for example Bombay was planned and re-developed so that by 1900 over three-quarters of India’s raw cotton were shipped through the city. Calcutta exported jute to Dundee while Madras sent coffee, sugar, indigo dyes and cotton to Britain.
cards.quote: In British India for example Bombay was planned and re-developed so that by 1900 over three-quarters of India’s raw cotton were shipped through the city. Calcutta exported jute to Dundee while Madras sent coffee, sugar, indigo dyes and cotton to Britain.

source.book: Social Change and Development in India
source.section: 1.2 Urbanisation and Industrialisation: The Colonial Experience

cards.subject: sociology
cards.unit: Process of Social Change in India
cards.front: Who leased three villages by the Hugli in 1690 to set up a trading post, from which Kolkata grew?
cards.back: In 1690, an English merchant named Job Charnock arranged to lease three villages (named Kolikata, Gobindapur, and Sutanuti) by the river Hugli in order to set up a trading post.
cards.quote: In 1690, an English merchant named Job Charnock arranged to lease three villages (named Kolikata, Gobindapur, and Sutanuti) by the river Hugli in order to set up a trading post.

cards.subject: sociology
cards.unit: Process of Social Change in India
cards.front: Types of urban impact on villages (M.S.A. Rao): the three situations.
cards.back:
Firstly, there are villages in which a sizeable number of people have sought employment in far-off cities.
The second kind of urban impact is to be seen in villages which are situated near an industrial town
The growth of metropolitan cities accounts for the third type of urban impact on the surrounding villages
cards.quote: Firstly, there are villages in which a sizeable number of people have sought employment in far-off cities. They live there leaving behind the members of their families in their natal villages. In Madhopur, a village in north central India, 77 out of 298 households have migrants, and a little less than half of all the migrants work in two cities of Bombay and Calcutta. About 75 percent of the total migrants send money regularly, and 83 per cent visit the village from four to five times a year to once in two years... A considerable number of emigrants reside not only in Indian cities but also in overseas towns. For instance, there are many overseas migrants from Gujarat villages living in African and British towns. They have built fashionable houses in their natal villages, invested money on land and industry, and have donated literally to the establishment of educational institutions and trusts... The second kind of urban impact is to be seen in villages which are situated near an industrial town...When an industrial town like Bhilai comes up in the midst of villages, some villages are totally uprooted while the lands of others are partially acquired. The latter are found to receive an influx of immigrant workers, which not only stimulates a demand for houses and a market inside the village but creates problems of ordering relationships between the native residents and the immigrants... ...The growth of metropolitan cities accounts for the third type of urban impact on the surrounding villages...While a few villages are totally absorbed in the process of expansion, only the land of many others, excluding the inhabited area, is used for urban development...

cards.front: What has happened for the first time since Independence in India's urban and rural population growth, and why?
